source_records.title: List all endpoints for MiniMax M2.7
source_records.subject: Exact public endpoint inventory, endpoint slugs, prices, status, and supported parameters
source_records.precise_paraphrase: The feed returned 14 endpoints. The first-party standard endpoint is minimax/fp8 at USD 0.30/M prompt, USD 1.20/M completion, and USD 0.06/M cache read; it advertises response_format but not structured_outputs.

source_records.title: OpenRouter Models API
source_records.subject: Model-level identity, aggregate pricing, and supported parameters
source_records.precise_paraphrase: The M2.7 record identifies canonical slug minimax/minimax-m2.7-20260318, aggregate USD 0.30/M prompt, USD 1.20/M completion, USD 0.06/M cache read, mandatory reasoning, response_format, and structured_outputs.

source_records.title: OpenRouter Zero Retention Endpoints API
source_records.subject: Current OpenRouter-asserted ZDR endpoint eligibility
source_records.precise_paraphrase: The feed contained 13 M2.7 endpoints, including minimax/fp8 and minimax/highspeed; this is OpenRouter's endpoint classification, not authenticated account evidence or a MiniMax contractual commitment.

source_records.title: Provider Routing
source_records.subject: Default routing, endpoint targeting, fallback, parameter, privacy, ZDR, and price controls
source_records.precise_paraphrase: Default routing balances across providers and fallbacks default true. Full endpoint slugs can target variants; only/order, allow_fallbacks false, require_parameters true, data_collection deny, zdr true, and max_price are documented filters. max_price prevents execution when no price-qualified endpoint is available.

source_records.title: Structured Outputs
source_records.subject: General json_schema strict-output contract and endpoint compatibility caveat
source_records.precise_paraphrase: Compatible routes accept response_format.type json_schema with strict true and schemas using additionalProperties false. The documentation directs callers to inspect model parameters and set require_parameters true; it does not prove the exact minimax/fp8 schema feature set.

source_records.title: Zero Data Retention
source_records.subject: OpenRouter ZDR meaning and enforcement layers
source_records.precise_paraphrase: OpenRouter defines ZDR as no provider storage for any period, supports account, guardrail, and per-request enforcement, and says provider.zdr true routes only to endpoints it classifies as ZDR. In-memory prompt caches are not considered retention by OpenRouter.

source_records.title: Data Collection
source_records.subject: OpenRouter content and metadata handling defaults
source_records.precise_paraphrase: OpenRouter says prompt/response storage and product-improvement use are opt-in and off by default. It stores request metadata without content and describes small anonymous prompt categorization using a ZDR model.

source_records.title: Provider Logging
source_records.subject: Upstream data-policy filtering and limits of router tags
source_records.precise_paraphrase: Provider data handling differs by endpoint. OpenRouter exposes training/data-policy filters and account settings, but its classifications reflect provider terms and do not replace upstream primary evidence.

source_records.title: OpenRouter API Reference Overview
source_records.subject: Request transformation, response usage, cost, and generation metadata
source_records.precise_paraphrase: OpenRouter normalizes and may transform parameters for upstream APIs. Non-streaming responses expose usage; generation records expose token counts, provider, and cost after completion. Public docs do not promise that pre-execution cost is final.

source_records.title: Router Metadata
source_records.subject: Observable routing identity and fail-closed filtering
source_records.precise_paraphrase: Opt-in metadata can show available and selected providers and per-attempt routing. A zero-attempt no-provider response can result when only or max_price filters remove all endpoints; some early and internal failures omit metadata, and cache hits strip it.

source_records.title: OpenRouter Frequently Asked Questions
source_records.subject: Inference pricing pass-through, credit-purchase fees, and BYOK fees
source_records.precise_paraphrase: OpenRouter says inference prices are passed through without markup. Credit purchases have a 5.5 percent fee with USD 0.80 minimum; BYOK has a separate threshold/fee. These are commercial/account mechanics, not an endpoint request fee.

source_records.title: OpenRouter Privacy Policy
source_records.subject: Router personal-data retention, third parties, and deletion
source_records.precise_paraphrase: The policy applies to OpenRouter, not upstream services; it uses necessity/legal-obligation retention rather than a fixed metadata period and provides deletion-request rights subject to exceptions.

source_records.title: MiniMax Pay as You Go Pricing
source_records.subject: First-party M2.7 list pricing
source_records.precise_paraphrase: MiniMax publishes USD 0.30/M input, USD 1.20/M output, USD 0.06/M prompt-cache read, and USD 0.375/M prompt-cache write for MiniMax-M2.7; the highspeed output rate is USD 2.40/M.

source_records.title: MiniMax API Privacy Policy
source_records.subject: MiniMax API personal-data purposes, vendors, transfers, security, and retention
source_records.precise_paraphrase: The policy permits service provision, improvement, security, and legal processing; describes vendors and cross-border processing, including US storage in the general policy; and uses necessity/legal criteria for retention. It does not publish a fixed API prompt/output retention period, exact M2.7 inference geography, or an unqualified no-training commitment.

source_records.title: MiniMax Terms of Service
source_records.subject: Client-data processing and applicable service rules
source_records.precise_paraphrase: MiniMax may access and process client data to provide the service, perform maintenance/support, and comply with law. Current platform service rules control pricing, privacy, and security; no endpoint-specific OpenRouter ZDR addendum is public here.

source_records.title: MiniMax M2.7
source_records.subject: Official model and first-party endpoint identity
source_records.precise_paraphrase: MiniMax documents standard M2.7 and M2.7-highspeed variants and the first-party API model identifier MiniMax-M2.7. It does not document OpenRouter route identity or strict JSON Schema guarantees.

model_level_aggregate_pricing.reason: Aggregate model pricing does not describe every endpoint and must not substitute for the exact endpoint record.

operational_cost_bands.purpose: Classify estimated bounded-operation cost; these bands are governance bands, not model-ranking scores.

future_customer_operation_economics.principle: Predictable bounded cost is more important than the lowest finite cost.

pricing_findings.pricing_drift_rule: Exact endpoint pricing drift must fail closed when it exceeds an approved ceiling.
pricing_findings.endpoint_selection_rule: An endpoint must not be selected merely because it is cheaper.
pricing_findings.cost_finality: post_generation_cost_is_the_auditable_value; no official guarantee found that preflight estimates are final

mutable_endpoint_snapshot.mara_rate_attribution: The captured official endpoint feed contained a row labeled mara with USD 0.24/M input and USD 0.96/M output; no separately captured official endpoint record supports a stronger provider-identity attribution.

endpoint_selection_framework.governance_rule: Pricing is the eighth criterion and is a bounded-cost gate, not a lowest-price ranking score.

preferred_for_controlled_test.reason: No candidate has complete evidence for the higher-ranked strict-output, privacy/ZDR, and latency criteria.

viable_alternative.reason: No alternative is yet supported across the ranked criteria.

requires_more_evidence.reason: The captured evidence is insufficient for a defensible final endpoint choice.

not_recommended.reason: Current evidence does not justify rejecting a candidate solely on price or incomplete evidence.

account_posture_findings.reason: No authenticated account export or screenshot was present or accessed.

structured_output_findings.require_parameters_expected_behavior: filters endpoints lacking requested parameter but does not prove semantic schema conformance

contradictions: The captured endpoint-feed row labeled mara reported USD 0.24/M input and USD 0.96/M output, while model-level metadata and the intended first-party endpoint were USD 0.30/M and USD 1.20/M; no stronger Mara provider attribution is made without a separately captured exact official endpoint record.
The model aggregate advertises structured_outputs, while the intended minimax/fp8 endpoint advertises response_format but not structured_outputs.
OpenRouter lists minimax/fp8 as ZDR, while MiniMax public policy and terms do not provide an endpoint-specific ZDR commitment or bounded prompt/output retention term.
